drug_class: Osmotic laxative / Lubricant and moisturizing agent (depending on use)
purpose: Polyethylene Glycol 400 (PEG 400) is used in two main ways. As eye drops, it helps relieve dry, irritated, or uncomfortable eyes by acting as an artificial tear. It is also used as an ingredient in some laxatives and skin products to help with moisture and lubrication.
how_it_works: When used in eye drops, PEG 400 coats the surface of your eye like a thin layer of moisture, helping to keep your eyes comfortable and reducing that dry, gritty feeling. When used as a laxative ingredient, it works by drawing water into your intestines, which softens your stool and makes it easier to pass. It basically works by holding onto water wherever it is applied.
common_side_effects: Eye drops: mild temporary stinging or blurring of vision right after use, which usually goes away quickly. Laxative use: bloating, gas, mild stomach cramps, nausea, or loose stools. These are usually mild and short-lived.
warnings: Do not use eye drops if you wear contact lenses unless the product says it is safe for contacts. Stop using and call your doctor if your eye pain gets worse, your vision changes, or redness continues. Do not use laxative forms for more than 1 week without talking to your doctor. Tell your doctor if you have kidney problems, as large amounts of PEG can affect fluid balance.
typical_dosing: For dry eye drops: usually 1 to 2 drops in the affected eye as needed, up to several times a day. For laxative products containing PEG: follow the directions on the package, typically once daily mixed in 4 to 8 ounces of liquid. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's specific instructions for your situation.
